Help us pass 1971 genocide resolution
2022-10-31T00:00:00+06:00 | Diplomatic Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/help-us-pass-1971-genocide-resolution-3156591

Genocide researchers and activists have called for the members of the Bangladeshi community across the US to engage with their legislators to have the genocide resolution on Bangladesh's Liberation War passed.

The call was made at a press conference organised by the Human Rights Congress for Bangladeshi Minorities (HRCBM) at the National Press Club in Washington DC on Saturday.

Speakers discussed the importance and implications of the bipartisan House Resolution "H. Res.1430 Recognizing the Bangladesh Genocide of 1971" that was introduced before the US Congress by the Congressmen Steve Chabot and Ro Khanna on October 14.

SM Alam, consul general of Bangladesh in Florida, appreciated the Congressmen for introducing the resolution and requested the members of the Bangladeshi diaspora to engage with other legislators to support the bill.

Columbia University lecturer and Genral Secretary (USA) of Bangladeshi Hindu Buddhist & Christian Unity Council, Dr Dwijen Bhattacharjya said introducing the resolution at the US Congress would encourage other nations to recognise the Bangladesh genocide of 1971.

In her opening remarks, HRCBM's executive director Priya Saha detailed how the Pakistani armed forces conducted one of the worst genocides in history over a period of nine months in 1971.

Journalist and freedom fighter Saleem Samad said Pakistani armed forces and its Bangladeshi allies employed rape as a tool of extermination in that horrible crime against humanity and urged everyone to recruit additional co-sponsors for the resolution.

Community leader Dilip Nath, Razzak Baloch of the Baloch Human Rights and Munawar Laghari, executive director of Sindhi Foundation; Adelle Nazarian, legislative director of the Hindu Pact, also spoke.
